dharana.sanskrit_iast: yadā mamecchā notpannā jñānaṃ vā kas tadāsmi vai | tattvato 'haṃ tathābhūtas tallīnas tanmanā bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 97: GRETIL encoding artefact '=B9' restored as avagraha: tattvato 'haṃ.
dharana.rendering: 'When no desire, and no knowing, has arisen in me, who am I then? In truth I am that, just as it is.' Absorbed in that, one's mind becomes one with it.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the desire, knowledge and activity of the ego are not those of the essential Self; when one realises and practises contemplation of the Self as pure consciousness-bliss, one rises above the ego and is dissolved in the essential Self. Wallis: 'I am as I am'.
dharana.technique_name: Who Am I Before Desire or Knowing Arise?
dharana.instruction: In a moment with no wanting and no thinking, ask 'who am I now?' and rest without answering in words.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 97 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the moment just before any wanting or knowing arises, and the question of what one is there.
geometry.svg_hint: a blank space just before a line begins
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Before anything arises
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the restless self that wants and knows is set aside, and simple being is noticed. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The state before any desire or knowing arises
attention.secondary: The question 'who am I then?' left open

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: 'When no desire, and no knowing, has arisen in me, who am I then? In truth I am that, just as it is.' Absorbed in that, one's mind becomes one with it.
adiyogi.method_summary: Rest until there is a moment with no particular want and no particular thought. Ask quietly: 'Who am I now?' Do not answer in words. Rest in what is there, just as it is.

honesty.disclosure: Door 074 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 74 (verse 97) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 074 is dharana 74, verse 97. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Leave the question open and light; it is not meant to be solved. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
